clue.text: Emphatically bad — no plaice available in town on the Fylde

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of the first word are spoilt and rearranged
no tells us the letters of the fish name are taken away from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A seaside town insists, emphatically, that its fish counter has run out of plaice.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: take PLAICE's letters out of EMPHATICALLY, which leaves MHTALY, and 'bad' rearranges them. The Fylde is a coastal plain in Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Lytham is a resort town on the Fylde coast of Lancashire, twinned with St Annes.

clue.text: Monthly tours include university in Devonshire resort

indicators.note: tours suggests the letters travel around into a new order
include adds the university letter to the pool being rearranged

explanation.surface: Monthly coach trips take in a university on the way to a Devon seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynmouth is a seaside village on the north Devon coast, long popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: What could be angriest city in Africa

indicators.note: What could be asks what the word angriest might become if its letters were rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks which African city is the angriest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangiers is a Moroccan port city on the Strait of Gibraltar, in north Africa.

clue.text: Two rivers shielded by a mountain city at Royal burgh

indicators.note: shielded by means the rivers sit protected inside the mountain letters

parts.note: Ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
R is the map abbreviation for river, and the Dee is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A Scottish burgh nestles where two rivers run beneath a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The rivers are R (the abbreviation) and DEE, which sit inside A BEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a Scottish city that holds the ancient status of a royal burgh.

clue.text: Work-room setback subsequently at Deeside resort

indicators.note: setback says the word for the work-room is set going backwards

parts.note: a lab, or laboratory, is a room for scientific work
subsequently means later, afterwards

explanation.surface: A setback at work is followed by a trip to a Scottish resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballater is a village and holiday resort on the River Dee in Aberdeenshire, near Balmoral.

clue.text: A long name for German city

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Someone wants a lengthy name for a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Aachen is a historic city in western Germany, Charlemagne's capital.

clue.text: Wreath on earth in Dutch city

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland or wreath of flowers
an earth is a fox's lair, also called a den

explanation.surface: A garland is laid on the ground in a Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: Leiden is a university city in the Netherlands, in South Holland.

clue.text: Drag act includes topless drag act in town in Co. Carlow

indicators.note: includes means the first drag word takes the second inside it

parts.note: towing is an act of dragging, a tow

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a pull is an act of dragging

explanation.surface: A drag show contains a topless drag act, in an Irish county town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag act' reads like cabaret, but it is just TOW and then PULL; 'topless' cuts PULL to ULL. County Carlow is in the south-east of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tullow is a market town in County Carlow, in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Arabian capital investment originally in Hardy novel

indicators.note: in places the initial letter inside the rearranged name
novel means new, so the letters of the name are arranged anew
originally points to the first letter of investment

explanation.surface: Capital investment from Arabia goes into a Thomas Hardy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy novel' looks like a book title, but 'novel' rearranges HARDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Determined grandma knocked back French port

indicators.note: knocked back means the joined words are read in reverse

parts.note: set means determined, as in set on doing something
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A determined grandmother is rebuffed at a French harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city and port on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: Host and family call round endlessly on mountain

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is the host of an event
kin are one's family

indicators.note: round means the shortened word is turned about
endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to yell is to call out

explanation.surface: A host and family call out as they go round a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' and 'round' both act on the call word: first cut, then turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount McKinley was the long-standing name of Denali, the highest peak in North America.

clue.text: Competed wearing spectacles, in Spanish city

indicators.note: wearing means the competing word sits inside the spectacles, as if wearing them

parts.note: two round lenses look like the letters OO
vied means competed

explanation.surface: Rivals wearing glasses compete in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is the capital of Asturias in northern Spain.

clue.text: Present way to cross breed of cattle

parts.note: here means present, in attendance
a ford is a shallow place where a river can be crossed

explanation.surface: A farmer shows a way to cross-breed cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross breed' reads as one idea, but 'cross' belongs to the wordplay and 'breed of cattle' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hereford is a red and white beef cattle breed from the English county of that name.

clue.text: Prince provided a cross for Canadian city

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
if means provided, on condition that
a cross is written as the letter X

explanation.surface: A prince offers a cross in return for a city in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Halifax is the capital of Nova Scotia, a city on Canada's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Turkish town and lake in the savannah

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie within the word savannah

explanation.surface: A Turkish town and lake sit out on the grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: Van is a town in eastern Turkey beside Lake Van, the country's largest lake.

clue.text: Might it be Brest, a capital of Bigorre

indicators.note: Might it be asks what the letters could become when shuffled

explanation.surface: Wonders whether the old capital of Bigorre might be the port of Brest.
explanation.walkthrough: Brest is a real French city, which makes it look like the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarbes was the historic capital of the county of Bigorre in south-west France.

clue.text: Female to prepare for future growth in Stafford's river

definitions.meaning: to plant seed so that it will grow
the river that flows through the town of Stafford

explanation.surface: Planting is under way on a farm by the river at Stafford.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple definition: a female pig, to plant seed, and the river flowing through Stafford.

clue.text: Engine part nearly arrived on university river

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: An engine part has almost reached the river at the university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge and its university.

clue.text: Dejected after All Saints' Day in Serbian city

indicators.note: after places the gloomy word following the date

parts.note: All Saints' Day falls on 1 November, written NOV I
sad means dejected, unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone feels low after the festival of All Saints.
explanation.definitionFit: Novi Sad is the second-largest city in Serbia, on the Danube.

clue.text: Brought back to conscious state in America

indicators.note: back means the word for brought is reversed

parts.note: led means brought, guided
aware means conscious

explanation.surface: A patient is brought back to consciousness in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the original thirteen states of the USA.

clue.text: It's unknown I'm with child outside in the country

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

indicators.note: outside puts the child word around the letter for with

parts.note: a babe is a baby, a young child

explanation.surface: A mysterious expectant mother speaks about living in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Zimbabwe is a landlocked nation in southern Africa.

clue.text: People feeling regret about old battle in 1356

indicators.note: about means the people word goes around the letter for old

parts.note: pitiers are people who feel pity or regret for others

explanation.surface: Mourners lament an old medieval battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Poitiers in 1356 was an English victory of the Hundred Years' War, led by the Black Prince.

clue.text: Come round about eleven in country

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the number
round turns the letters of come about into a new order

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, also a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Someone is invited round at about eleven in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is a nation in North America, south of the United States.

clue.text: Rankin going round wicked Nigerian state capital

indicators.note: going round means the first name surrounds the wicked word

parts.note: Ian Rankin is the Scottish crime writer
bad means wicked

explanation.surface: A crime novelist tours a wicked city in Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is the capital of Oyo State and one of Nigeria's largest cities.

clue.text: City centre of Leibnitz occupied by army corps

indicators.note: occupied by means the corps moves into the central letters
centre of picks the two middle letters of the philosopher's name

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An army corps takes over the town where Leibnitz worked.
explanation.definitionFit: Bremen is a port city and city-state in north-west Germany.

clue.text: Exercise with oxygen with fresh air at Illinois port

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: fresh means the letters of air are made anew

explanation.surface: Exercising with oxygen and fresh air at a port in Illinois.
explanation.definitionFit: Peoria is a city on the Illinois River, a historic river port in that state.

clue.text: Marble from Devonshire river

definitions.meaning: a large playing marble used for shooting at others
a river of north Devon flowing into Barnstaple Bay

explanation.surface: A marble is fished out of a river in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fair: a shooting marble in the game of marbles, and the River Taw in north Devon.

clue.text: Formal dress in town in Orange County

definitions.meaning: a dinner jacket, as the Americans call it
a town in Orange County, New York, where the jacket got its name

explanation.surface: Black tie is required at an event in Orange County.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinner jacket was named after Tuxedo Park, in the town of Tuxedo, New York State.

clue.text: Carried money, reportedly for wine

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is spoken and heard

parts.note: bore means carried; dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone carried cash, so the story goes, to buy wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is the red or white wine from the region around that French city.

clue.text: Village near Loch Lomond of shooting star — Bethlehem?

indicators.note: of shooting suggests the letters shoot out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Scottish village is named after the star that guided the wise men.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'star' and the start of 'Bethlehem'; the dash is punctuation and is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarbet is a village on the western shore of Loch Lomond in Argyll and Bute.

clue.text: Royal burgh charges keeping firm in trouble

indicators.note: keeping means the charges word holds the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: dues are charges or fees

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters of firm are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A town levies charges that keep a struggling firm afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumfries is a Scottish town in the south-west that holds the status of a royal burgh.

clue.text: South coast river through the heart of York's historic street

indicators.note: the heart of keeps only the inside of the street name, dropping its two outer letters

parts.note: The Shambles is a famous medieval street in York

explanation.surface: A river runs through the middle of a historic street in York.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hamble is a short river in Hampshire flowing into Southampton Water on England's south coast.

clue.text: The food's untouched, we're told, in Warwickshire town

indicators.note: we're told means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: if the food is untouched then none has been eaten

explanation.surface: A diner reports the food lying untouched in a Midlands town.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuneaton is a market town in the north of Warwickshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: North-east, towards French capital of department

parts.note: vers is the French word for towards

explanation.surface: Heading north-east towards a French regional capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevers is the prefecture, or administrative centre, of the Nièvre department in central France.
